question: What does OOB stand for in random forests and what fraction of rows is out-of-bag for each tree?
answer: OOB stands for out-of-bag in random forests. [S1] About 36.8% of the rows are out-of-bag for each tree. [S1]

citations.title: Ml Notation Abbreviations
citations.text: OOB: out-of-bag. In a random forest each tree is trained on a bootstrap sample, and the rows left out of that sample are the out-of-bag rows; about 36.8% (1/e) of the rows are out-of-bag for each tree. They provide a free validation estimate. MAE: mean absolute error. RMSE: root mean squared error. SGD: stochastic gradient descent. k-NN: k-nearest neighbors. PR AUC: area under the precision-recall curve; preferred over ROC AUC for strongly imbalanced classes. i.i.d.: independent and identically distributed. precision: in classification, TP / (TP + FP). It is not the same as measurement precision in statistics. sample: in machine learning a sample usually means one row of data (one example). In statistics a sample is a subset of a population. bias: the error from wrong assumptions of a model. The bias term (intercept) of a linear model is a different thing.

S2.title: Ml Exercise Guide
S2.text:
Assignment 1: Diagnosing a Model
Task. You trained a decision tree classifier and obtained 99% training accuracy but 71% validation accuracy. Explain what is happening and propose two fixes.
Expected answer. The large gap between training and validation accuracy is the signature of overfitting (high variance). Fixes include limiting the maximum depth of the tree, requiring a minimum number of samples per leaf, pruning, switching to a random forest, or collecting more data. Report validation performance using cross-validation rather than a single split.

Common algorithms: linear regression, logistic regression, k-nearest neighbors (classifies by the  majority label among the k closest examples), decision trees (split data using feature thresholds; deep trees overfit), random forests (many decorrelated trees averaged to reduce variance) and gradient boosting (trees added sequentially to correct earlier errors).

S5.title: Ml Model Diagnostics Handbook
S5.text:
4. Class Imbalance and Validation Practice
For imbalanced classification set class_weight='balanced' so that rare classes receive a larger
weight in the loss, or resample the training folds. Oversampling must be done inside each training
fold only; oversampling before splitting leaks duplicated rows into the validation fold. Report the
precision-recall curve or F1 rather than accuracy.
A common validation setup is StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42). The
helper cross_val_score(estimator, X, y, cv=5, scoring='f1') returns one score per fold. For time
series use TimeSeriesSplit so that the training data always come before the validation data.
